CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
1. Region means Wonosobo Regency.
2. Regional Government means the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration.
3. Regent means the Regent of Wonosobo.
4. Vice Regent means the Vice Regent of Wonosobo.
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD means the Regional House of Representatives of Wonosobo Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD means the Apparatus of Wonosobo Regency tasked in the field of social protection and social welfare administration for women and children.
7. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD means part of SKPD.
8. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so that they can live properly and are able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions.
9. Social welfare administration for women and children is a directed, integrated, and sustainable effort carried out by the Government, Regional Government and community in the form of social services to meet the basic needs of every citizen, especially women and children, which includes social rehabilitation, social security, social empowerment, and social protection.
10. Social problems
11. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out their social functions properly in community life.
12. Social empowerment is all efforts directed to enable citizens experiencing social problems to have power, so that they are able to meet their basic needs.
13. Social security is an institutionalized scheme to guarantee all people so that they can meet their basic life needs properly.
14. Social protection is all efforts directed to prevent and handle risks from social problems.
15. Special protection is
16. Social outreach is a series of activities to pick up women and children who are in parks, markets, streets and public places that can cause social problems, so that these women and children receive social welfare administration services.
17. Social organization is a social association formed by the community whether legally incorporated or not legally incorporated that functions as a means of community participation in carrying out social welfare efforts.
18. Social Institution is an institution or work unit established by the community and or government that provides social welfare services.
19. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (Eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
20. Child in emergency situation is
21. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially.
22. Child with disability is a child who experiences physical and or mental障碍 so that their growth and development is disrupted normally.
23. Child welfare is a child's life that can guarantee their growth and development properly both physically, spiritually and socially.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
25. Poor family is a family that does not have a source of livelihood and does not have the ability to meet basic needs that are proper for humanity or people who have a source of livelihood but cannot meet proper basic needs.
26. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
27. Human trafficking is
28. Victim is
29. Person with disability is every person who has physical and or mental abnormalities that can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to perform properly, consisting of persons with physical and mental disabilities.
30. Social deviant is a person whose life does not conform to religious norms, moral norms, legal norms, and or community norms.
31. Care is various efforts given to children who do not have parents and are neglected, neglected children, and children experiencing behavioral problems, which are temporary in nature as a substitute for parents or family so that they can grow and develop properly both spiritually, physically, and socially.
32. Social assistance is assistance that is not permanent or temporary in nature and is given within a certain period of time to social welfare beneficiaries who are unable so that they can improve their social welfare level and are able to carry out their social functions properly in community life both spiritually, physically, and socially.
33. Community members are residents of Wonosobo Regency and foreign citizens residing in Wonosobo Regency.
34. Community is a group of community members who have attention and a role in the field of social welfare.
35. Violence against children is

Article 3
a. A neglected child is a child aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poverty/inability, one or both parents/guardians being ill or deceased, family disharmony), cannot have their basic needs properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually or socially.
b. A child who is a victim of gender-based violence or maltreatment is a child aged 0-18 years who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, maltreatment or improper treatment within the family environment or immediate social environment, so that their basic needs cannot be properly fulfilled, whether physically, spiritually or socially.
c. A delinquent child is a child aged 0-18 years who behaves in deviation from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their family and others, and will disturb public order, but due to age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.
d. A street child is a child aged 0-18 years who spends most of their time seeking livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.
e. A child with disabilities is a child aged 0-18 years who has physical and/or mental abnormalities, which can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to carry out activities normally, consisting of those with physical disabilities, those with mental disabilities, those with physical and mental disabilities.
f. A woman vulnerable to socio-economic conditions is an adult woman aged 18-59 years, unmarried or widowed, who does not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.
g. A woman who is a victim of gender-based violence and/or maltreatment is a woman aged 18-59 years who is threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to acts of violence, maltreatment or improper treatment within the family environment or immediate social environment.
h. Trafficking of women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to then be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment

Article 7
Social protection for women and children aims to:
a. eliminate all forms of violence against women and children
b. protect, provide a sense of security for women and children
c. improve the standard of welfare, quality, and continuity of life.
d. restore social functions in order to achieve independence.
e. increase social resilience of the community in preventing and addressing social welfare issues.
f. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business sector in the implementation of social welfare in an institutionalized and sustainable manner.
g. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business sector and community.

Article 34
(1) Research, monitoring and evaluation as referred to in Article 30 letter d, shall be conducted in the framework of evaluating the social impact of development, policy development and achievement of social welfare objectives.
(2) Research, monitoring, and evaluation shall be implemented periodically or according to needs by SKPD/UKPD in accordance with their functions and authorities.

BAB II
SCOPE
Article 2
The scope of social protection includes: women and children with social problems.

Article 28
Paragraph (1) Social organizations include community organizations, non-governmental organizations, social rehabilitation centers for persons with disabilities organized by social bodies, social organizations that can operate care services for abandoned children Paragraph (2) Sufficiently Clear Paragraph (3) Sufficiently Clear Paragraph (4) Sufficiently Clear Paragraph (5) Sufficiently Clear Paragraph (6) For the sake of legal and social order, Social Organizations must have legal entity status because they have important duties and functions and their existence and work programs must be accountable. The Regent as regional head who is responsible for social issues has authority in the field of licensing.
Paragraph 7 Sufficiently Clear

CHAPTER VIII
ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS
Article 38
(1) Every social organization that has obtained a permit in the implementation of social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children, which deliberately does not provide social services as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (5), may be subject to administrative sanctions.
(2) Every social organization that implements social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children without a permit as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (6), may be subject to administrative sanctions.
(3) Administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1), may be in the form of: a. verbal warning;
b. written warning;
c. revocation of permit.

Article 18
(1) Every child has the right to obtain social protection and the implementation of social welfare from parents, family, community, and regional government to grow and develop properly.
(2) Every child has the right to obtain social protection and the implementation of social welfare to develop their abilities and social life in accordance with the culture and personality of the nation to become a good and useful member of society.
(3) Every child has the right to obtain maintenance of the child's welfare level and protection from environments that endanger and/or hinder their growth and development properly.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF WONOSOBO REGENCY
NUMBER 2 YEAR 2012
CONCERNING
SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The target of development in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation is directed towards Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is adjusted to the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as to provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, that in efforts to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation concerning Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and so that it is formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must pay attention to environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed necessary as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government, specifically the Wonosobo Regional Government, to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF WONOSOBO REGENCY
NUMBER 2 YEAR 2012
CONCERNING
SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The target of development in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation is directed towards Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is adjusted to the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as to provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, that in efforts to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation concerning Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and so that it is formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must pay attention to environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed necessary as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government, specifically the Wonosobo Regional Government, to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The target of development in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation is directed towards Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is adjusted to the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as to provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, that in efforts to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation concerning Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and so that it is formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must pay attention to environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed necessary as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government, specifically the Wonosobo Regional Government, to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

Article 4

b. Social advocacy; and/or
c. legal assistance.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The target of development in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation is directed towards Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is adjusted to the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as to provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, that in efforts to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation concerning Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and so that it is formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must pay attention to environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed necessary as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government, specifically the Wonosobo Regional Government, to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The target of development in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation is directed towards Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is adjusted to the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as to provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, that in efforts to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation concerning Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and so that it is formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must pay attention to environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

Third Part
Social Protection And Implementation of Social Welfare For Children

Article 7
Social protection for women and children aims to:
a. eliminate all forms of violence against women and children
b. protect, provide a sense of security for women and children
c. improve the standard of welfare, quality, and continuity of life.
d. restore social functions in order to achieve independence.
e. increase social resilience of the community in preventing and addressing social welfare issues.
f. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business sector in the implementation of social welfare in an institutionalized and sustainable manner.
g. increase awareness, capability, concern and social responsibility of the business sector and community.

e. I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The target of development in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation is directed towards Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is adjusted to the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as to provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, that in efforts to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation concerning Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and so that it is formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must pay attention to environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The target of development in the field of social welfare regulated in this Regional Regulation is directed towards Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is adjusted to the objectives and functions of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for efforts of Social Protection for Women and Children as well as to provide studies within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework regarding the necessity of a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for handling social problems in Wonosobo Regency, especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, that in efforts to overcome the problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation concerning Social Protection for Women and Children which essentially constitutes action that is rooted in or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and so that it is formulated with correct principles.

The regulation of the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must pay attention to environmental aspects and social aspects, so that the social conditions of the community are controlled. The regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulation can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a Regional Regulation that specifically regulates Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed necessary as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government, specifically the Wonosobo Regional Government, to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.
